body.statement: For the threshold sequence \(\varepsilon_n=3\sqrt{\mu^\star\log(n)/n}\), with \(p,k,L,B,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}\) fixed, \[\sup_{\substack{\|\beta\|_2\le B,\;\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\\ \text{admissible conditional-noise laws}}}\left|\frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon_n)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}-1\right|\longrightarrow0.\]
body.justification: This establishes that the exact population \(A\)-risk is attained uniformly over the stated fixed-dimensional coefficient and noise class.
body.gap: PFED gives near-optimal passive-risk control, whereas this statement isolates the all-order limited-supply oracle constant and its exact leverage-dependent threshold.
body.consumer: The result justifies replacing numerical population design search by the uniform dosage in sufficiently large independent-delivery screens.
body.proof_tex:
Under the fixed-dimensional assumption, \(q\), \(\mu^\star\), and \(\Phi^\star\) are fixed positive constants. For all sufficiently large \(n\), the condition \(n>36\mu^\star\log n\) holds and
\[
 \varepsilon_n=3\sqrt{\frac{\mu^\star\log n}{n}}<\frac12,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
The risk theorem gives
\[
 b_{n,\varepsilon_n}
 \le2q\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n\varepsilon_n^2}{3\mu^\star}\right\}
 =2qn^{-3}. \tag{8}
\]
For an admissible \((\beta,\sigma)\), set
\[
 \rho_n(\beta,\sigma)
 =\frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon_n)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}.
\]
This is well defined because \(\sigma\ge\sigma_{\min}>0\) and \(\Phi^\star\ge1\). Dividing the two-sided risk bound by its oracle scale gives
\[
 \frac{1-b_{n,\varepsilon_n}}{1+\varepsilon_n}
 \le\rho_n(\beta,\sigma)
 \le\frac1{1-\varepsilon_n}
 +\frac{nB^2}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}b_{n,\varepsilon_n}.
\]
The lower endpoint is below one by at most \(\varepsilon_n+b_{n,\varepsilon_n}\), and the first term of the upper endpoint exceeds one by at most \(2\varepsilon_n\). Uniformly over the stated coefficient ball, variance range, and all conditional-noise laws satisfying the two moment assumptions, (8) therefore yields
\[
 \left|\rho_n(\beta,\sigma)-1\right|
 \le2\varepsilon_n+2qn^{-3}
 +\frac{2B^2q}{\sigma_{\min}^2\Phi^\star}n^{-2}.
\]
The right-hand side is deterministic and tends to zero. Taking the displayed supremum proves the asserted uniform oracle attainment. Because the argument treats \(\mu^\star\) as fixed, it makes no growing-dimension or vanishing-supply uniformity claim.
